text: 1946: ENIAC, one of the first general-purpose electronic computers, was unveiled to the public.
1948: The Manchester Baby ran the first program stored in electronic memory.
1947: A moth found in Harvard's Mark II relay gave 'debugging' its most famous logbook entry.
1969: The first ARPANET message was sent from UCLA to SRI. It was meant to say 'LOGIN' and crashed after 'LO'.
1968: Douglas Engelbart demonstrated the mouse, hypertext and video conferencing in 'the Mother of All Demos'.
1971: The first edition of the Unix Programmer's Manual was published.
1973: Bob Metcalfe wrote the memo that described Ethernet.
1975: Microsoft was founded in Albuquerque by Bill Gates and Paul Allen.
1976: Apple Computer was founded by Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak and Ronald Wayne.
1981: IBM introduced the IBM Personal Computer, model 5150.
1983: ARPANET switched to TCP/IP, the foundation of today's Internet.
1989: Tim Berners-Lee circulated his proposal for what became the World Wide Web.
1991: The first public web site, info.cern.ch, went live.
1991: Linus Torvalds announced his hobby operating system, later named Linux.
1993: id Software released Doom as shareware.
